svg.title: The assistant loop — okfy algorithm explainer
svg.desc: How one question is answered by a bounded loop of requests and tool calls. The turn opens with the user's question and runs at most eight requests. Each request carries the replayed messages, the fixed tool schema, an automatic tool choice and optionally streaming; the reply is pushed as an assistant message, and when it carries no tool calls the turn ends there. When it carries tool calls, a reply is reserved for every call in the same synchronous step as the call, before any tool runs, so a message that arrives mid-turn, such as a user bubble the microphone opens, can never land between a tool-call message and its replies, which providers require them to follow; a tool that throws still answers its call, so the history stays valid. A thinking-mode model's reasoning is kept on every tool-call message and sent on the next request, and the field is present on every such message, an empty string rather than an omitted field, because those providers reject the next request otherwise. When the step cap is reached the turn does not end on an error: one further request goes out with the tools withheld, so the model closes with an answer about what it found, and an error stands only if that closing answer fails. The replayed history is trimmed so a long session cannot grow without bound: every message is kept, but only the most recent eight tool results are sent in full and an older one is shortened to a leading excerpt rather than dropped to a placeholder, and reasoning from older tool-call rounds is shortened to two thousand characters while the most recent round's reasoning is kept whole so a thinking-mode model can continue it. When the prompt still passes three quarters of the model's context length the conversation is compacted: one capped request summarizes the older turns, the replay resumes at the sixth most recent user turn with the newer turns verbatim, and the summary rides into the prompt as a system message, marked in the transcript by a notice; the summary's own tokens count toward the session total but not toward the per-request readings. The request is otherwise bounded like any other read, with a deadline and a streamed-byte cap, and the bundle is treated as untrusted: the system prompt tells the model to treat concept text and tool results as data and never as instructions, so a hostile concept cannot redirect the agent.

One question runs a bounded loop of requests and tool calls
the loop runs again until a reply carries no tool calls
At the 8-step cap the turn does not end on an error: one more request goes out with the tools withheld,
so the model closes with an answer about what it found.
A tool-call message and its replies are never split
a reply is pushed for every call in the same synchronous step as the call
a tool that throws still answers its call, so the history stays valid
a message mid-turn — the microphone can open a bubble — cannot land between them
a thinking-mode trace is kept on every tool-call message, empty rather than absent
Providers require each tool-call message to be followed by exactly its replies; the loop keeps that order.
Every message is kept; only what is replayed is bounded
the most recent 8 tool results are replayed in full
shortened to a leading excerpt — never dropped to a content-free placeholder
trimmed to 2 000 characters, so a long trace cannot crowd the prompt
kept whole, so a thinking-mode model can continue it
Trimming the replay is what keeps a long session from growing without bound while the thread survives.
Past 75 % of the context length, the older turns are summarized
The replay resumes at the sixth most recent user turn, so a tool call is never separated from its replies.
The summary's own tokens count toward the session total, not toward the per-request readings.
The loop is capped, and the bundle is treated as untrusted
8 requests, then one closing request with the tools withheld
8 000 input characters; each tool result is capped at 12 000
a 120 s deadline, and 4 MiB of streamed reply
its text and tool results are data, never instructions to follow
a token budget stops a new question once it is spent
A hostile concept cannot redirect the agent: the tools only read the graph or drive the viewer.
The loop is what makes the assistant an agent: it decides which tools to call, and the viewer bounds each step
